Current Technology Adoption.summary: Core platform capabilities established; data usage improved and early use cases validated via Lighthouse Programmes. Future focus on deeper integration, wider adoption, and greater reuse across the enterprise to strengthen business enablement.

Digital Transformation.summary: Digital innovation drives operational efficiency and customer engagement; 97‑98% of financial transactions are digital, with digital channels contributing 20‑60% across key journeys. The bank invests in digital modernisation, data, automation, and GenAI.

R&D.summary: R&D remains largely in‑house, supported by partnerships with technology ecosystems, fintechs, start‑ups, and academia. Employees increasingly use AI‑enabled tools to reduce manual effort and improve productivity. Environmental and social impact metrics are tracked within R&D and capex investments.

Emerging Technologies.summary: AI powers advanced customer analytics, personalised communication, and behavioural insights. End‑to‑end digital products expand reach among younger, mobile‑first customers, creating a simpler, faster, safer, and more intelligent digital environment. In‑house technology franchise enhances resilience and innovation.

Technology Partnerships.summary: Partnerships with technology ecosystems, academia, fintechs, and start‑ups complement in‑house engineering strengths, supporting core platform development and digital innovation that improves stakeholder engagement and accessibility.

Technology Investments.summary: Investments in infrastructure, including data centre enhancements and cloud alignment, improve performance, security, and scalability. The bank’s extensive physical reach is supported by a strong, reliable digital foundation, ensuring continuity across onboarding, servicing, and support.

Cloud Adoption.summary: Core systems modernised for scale and resilience, with cloud alignment and infrastructure enhancements improving availability, security, and performance. Digital ecosystem upgrades to MobileBanking, NetBanking, website, and payments infrastructure support these improvements.

Automation.summary: Automation enhances customer engagement through real‑time interactions, streamlines card processing and trade operations, strengthens risk oversight with intelligent monitoring, and empowers employees by automating routine tasks. Neev, the in‑house AI platform, underpins these workflows.

Cybersecurity.summary: A comprehensive cybersecurity governance framework includes policy, incident management, and crisis plans, supported by tabletop exercises. The bank complies with ISO 27001:2022, ISO 22301:2019, and PCI DSS, and implements a multi‑layered security strategy to protect personal information.

Future Technology Roadmaps.summary: The bank accelerates fully digital and STP‑led onboarding across all product lines, expands end‑to‑end digital products for younger customers, and strengthens digital capability through focused collaboration and learning interventions.

Technology Pain Areas.summary: Key technology risks include use and operation of IT systems, system availability and performance, cyber and information security threats, and third‑party/vendor dependencies.

AI.summary: AI is deployed across the organization to deliver faster, consistent customer responses, improve credit decisioning, and enable AI‑assisted trade classification. Neev, the in‑house AI platform, provides a secure foundation for model access, governance, and workflow integration.

Tech Risk.summary: Technology risk areas mirror those in Technology Pain Areas: IT system use and operation, system availability and performance, cyber and information security threats, and third‑party/vendor dependencies.

Platforms & Systems.summary: Enterprise‑scale AI foundations are established with Neev, an in‑house AI platform offering unified model access, security, workflows, and data integration. Core platform capabilities are validated through Lighthouse Programmes, with future focus on deeper integration and reuse. Infrastructure investments enhance performance and security.

Talent & Skills.summary: Enterprise‑wide programmes upskill technical, functional, and behavioural competencies, increasing average learning hours per employee. Training, workplace platforms, and tech‑enabled HR processes improve productivity and service quality, while regular cyber drills reinforce a strong cybersecurity culture.

Current Technology Adoption.summary: The company is investing in backward integration, domestic capacity creation, technology adoption, and sustainable manufacturing to reduce dependence on imported key starting materials and improve supply resilience. Rising regulatory expectations and compliance costs reinforce entry barriers, favoring scaled, quality‑focused players with strong governance and manufacturing systems.

R&D.summary: Innovation focuses on practical, lifecycle‑driven R&D, emphasizing processes that simplify manufacturing, reduce environmental impact, and maintain efficiency. The company’s own R&D centres develop technologies for active pharmaceutical ingredients and intermediates, which are implemented in manufacturing, enhancing compliance, reducing variability, and improving cost efficiency.

Emerging Technologies.summary: The company’s R&D centres develop and implement technologies for active pharmaceutical ingredients and intermediates, continuously reviewing and optimizing processes. These efforts lower production costs, enable consistent exports, and strengthen competitiveness in the global market.

Technology Partnerships.summary: The company relies on bilateral and regional trade partnerships and supplier diversification to mitigate concentration risks, evolving procurement toward risk‑adjusted frameworks prioritising supply assurance and compliance. Its Custom Synthesis business, serving global innovators, contributes over half of revenues, underscoring the importance of chemistry‑led collaboration and ESG considerations in supplier selection.

Technology Investments.summary: Software maintenance costs are expensed as incurred. Intangible assets carried at 1st April 2015 GAAP values are used as deemed cost under Ind AS. Research and development expenses are fully charged to expense in the period incurred, with uncertainties in new product development precluding capitalization.

Cybersecurity.summary: Information security systems are constantly tested, updated, and expanded, supported by employee training on data protection and secure online banking. The company implements EDR, endpoint and server protection, automated prevention and detection, perimeter security, web security tools, enhanced vulnerability detection, and network segmentation based on business criticality. Enterprise‑wide risk management oversees cybersecurity alongside business, regulatory, ESG, and operational risks.

Technology Pain Areas.summary: Commercial success now requires effective lifecycle management across indication expansion, combination therapies, and sustained market access. Rising R&D costs and longer development timelines make operational reliability across the supply chain critical to preserving commercial value.

Tech Risk.summary: The company has a comprehensive business continuity framework to mitigate disruptive events, employing alternative solutions to reduce damage. Sustainable operations are pursued by assessing risks of sourcing and manufacturing, implementing optimal processes to minimize or de‑risk operations. An IT policy ensures data and system protection, with continuous testing and updates of security systems.

Talent & Skills.summary: The company offers a rewarding work environment with career development opportunities, extensive training programs to enhance skills and expertise, and a focus on employee well-being and professional growth.

Current Technology Adoption.summary: Scaled AI, machine learning, IoT and advanced analytics across factories to enhance process stability, energy efficiency and asset reliability, including predictive‑maintenance platforms that use IoT sensors and AI models to reduce unplanned downtime. Advanced process control systems and AI‑driven optimisation were deployed on kilns and mills, supported by connected‑worker, robotics and computer‑vision technologies. Cloud‑based data services and the SAP S/4HANA RISE programme were initiated to improve scalability and system resilience.

Digital Transformation.summary: SAP S/4HANA upgrade and the RISE programme transition core ERP to cloud, while Speed 2.0 optimises order allocation. RMC Control Tower provides real‑time scheduling and mobile collaboration across plants. Invoice‑to‑Payment revamp streamlines high‑volume transactions, and UltraBuddy, a WhatsApp‑based GenAI assistant, offers 24×7 dealer support.

R&D.summary: In‑house R&D FY 2025‑26: ₹4.07 cr capital, ₹15.38 cr recurring, total ₹19.45 cr. Scientific research contribution ₹7.50 cr, bringing total FY 2025‑26 R&D to ₹26.95 cr (0.03 % of turnover). FY 2024‑25 R&D was ₹29.14 cr (0.04 % of turnover). R&D priorities focus on environmental footprint, operational efficiency and next‑generation materials.

Emerging Technologies.summary: AI‑driven predictive maintenance combines IoT sensor data with machine‑learning models to forecast failures. Thousands of IoT sensors capture real‑time operational signals. Robotics, computer‑vision, drones and advanced sensing are deployed to automate inspection, enhance safety and support Industry 4.0 initiatives.

Technology Partnerships.summary: SAP ERP deployment consolidates material codes and audit readiness. Collaboration with GCCA Innovandi network advances low‑carbon cement and operational efficiency. Third‑party agencies strengthen ESG assessment and digital procurement analytics. VendX digital procurement platform automates sourcing workflows.

Technology Investments.summary: Intangible assets under development rose to Rs 28.41 cr as of 1 Apr 2024, with additions of Rs 61.62 cr in FY 2024‑25, reaching Rs 45.92 cr by 31 Mar 2025 and Rs 466.40 cr by 31 Mar 2026. Rs 211.54 cr added to capital work‑in‑progress, potentially covering technology acquisitions.

Cloud Adoption.summary: SAP S/4HANA RISE migrates core ERP to cloud, improving scalability. A robust Data Warehouse and Data Lake underpin AI, ML, GenAI, IoT and analytics. DSPM services and CrowdStrike Spotlight enhance cloud security. No monetary cloud spend disclosed.

Automation.summary: Robotics, drones and sensor‑based technologies boost resilience, safety and sustainability. Online workflow for credit‑exception approvals reduces paperwork. AI‑driven predictive maintenance and advanced process control improve uptime and process consistency.

Cybersecurity.summary: Framework includes real‑time intrusion alerts, decoys, backups and continuous monitoring. OT security reinforced via patch‑management, intrusion‑detection and antivirus. IT‑OT micro‑segmentation completed across additional plants; secure remote access standardised for 23 units. Steering and Board committees oversee cyber‑risk management.

Future Technology Roadmaps.summary: Near‑term roadmap scales Agentic AI, robotics and advanced analytics globally. SAP S/4HANA RISE continues cloud transition. RMC Control Tower pilots dynamic scheduling and real‑time visibility. DataPulse, an in‑house GenAI BI platform, delivers real‑time insights. AI and automation scaling planned across all functions.

Technology Pain Areas.summary: Skilled manpower shortage and limited leadership talent destabilise operations. Sub‑optimal AI adoption due to capability gaps and lack of responsible‑AI governance. Rapid cyber‑threat evolution and generative‑AI data exposure risk breaches. Integration between IT and OT requires strengthening, leading to micro‑segmentation and remote‑access standardisation.

AI.summary: Scaled AI and ML models for predictive maintenance using IoT data improve uptime. AI‑driven optimisation on kilns and mills boosts efficiency and fuel utilisation. Computer‑vision and robotics enhance inspection and safety. Proprietary GenAI engine expands predictive‑maintenance capabilities. Continued investment in in‑house and OEM platforms supports AI‑enabled asset monitoring.

Tech Risk.summary: Cyber‑risk strategy focuses on proactive prevention, early detection and rapid response with advanced vulnerability tools and auto‑remediation. CrowdStrike Spotlight enhances endpoint visibility. DSPM services continuously identify cloud risks. Application‑level microsegmentation limits lateral threat movement. Controls restrict public GenAI platform use to mitigate data exposure.

Platforms & Systems.summary: MineOptima360 integrates mining value chain, delivering measurable productivity gains and scaling across units. Centralised Mines Analytics Dashboard tracks key operational and cost indicators. SAP S/4HANA RISE transitions core ERP to cloud. RMC Control Tower enables dynamic scheduling and real‑time visibility. Data Warehouse and Data Lake underpin AI, ML, GenAI, IoT and analytics.

Talent & Skills.summary: Delivered 9,503,388 training hours, averaging Rs 4,840 per employee. Offered 11,158 distinct programmes covering leadership, technical, safety and digital tools. Upgraded skills for over 17,000 employees. Learning ecosystem structured around Fit to Work, Fit to Perform and Fit to Grow pillars.
